recent_candidates.title: A Plea to the Next Congress
recent_candidates.author: Luke Nicastro
recent_candidates.excerpt: Congress A Plea to the Next Congress Do something, anything! Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images In Virginia, Election Day dawned as beautiful as is possible for early November, perfectly embodying the “mellow fruitfulness” assigned by Keats to this most wonderful of seasons. I write having just returned from my local polling place, where the mild autumn weather combined with a tableau of civic participation—a PTA bake sale, cordial representatives of both parties smilingly manning their respective booths—to produce an archetypically American scene. Yet all is not well in our republic. By the time you read this, control of Congress should be clear; and unless the polls have been spectacularly off, at least the House will have been carried by insurgent Dems capitalizing on popular fury over, inter alia , the cost of living and the ongoing Iran imbroglio (my own low-conviction guess for the Senate is a 50–50 tie). [Editor’s Note: It was in fact a bloodbath for Republicans on all fronts.] Whatever the precise balance of forces, there is an urgent and unfortunately herculean task at hand for the next batch of lawmakers. This is nothing less than the resuscitation of their institution: The rescue of Congress from the impotence and disgrace into which it has latterly sunk. I should say here that I don’t expect the 120th Congress to accomplish this work. But I would be remiss in my duties as a columnist if I failed to give appealing to the civic sense of our newly-elected representatives

recent_candidates.excerpt: The Democratic candidate Annie Andrews defeated the Republican incumbent Sen. Darline Graham in Tuesday’s South Carolina senatorial election. recent_candidates.title: Musk’s Minnesota Deepfake Fight Could Define AI’s First Amendment
recent_candidates.author: Jeff Kosseff
recent_candidates.excerpt: A rapidly developing legal battle between Elon Musk and the state of Minnesota may soon clarify some of the First Amendment’s limits on the government’s ability to regulate artificial intelligence (AI). The dispute stems from a very real online harm—deepfake nude images—but Minnesota addressed the problem in a way that some say the First Amendment prohibits. Last spring, Minnesota’s legislature, in a nearly unanimous vote, passed HF 1606 , titled “Prohibition on Nudification Technology.” The law enables the state attorney general to seek up to $500,000 in fines from a technology company each time that company allows “a user to access, download, or use the website, application, software, program, or other service to nudify an image or video” or to “nudify an image or video on behalf of a user.” The law broadly defines “nudify” as altering or generating a video or image “to depict an intimate part not depicted in an original unaltered image or video of an identifiable individual” provided that the image or video “is so realistic that a reasonable person would believe that the intimate part belongs to the identifiable individual.” Many states—including Minnesota—already have nonconsensual intimate imagery laws , and some of those laws already cover deepfakes. But these laws impose civil or criminal penalties on the people who created or distributed the images. What makes Minnesota’s new law different is that it places legal responsibility on the company whose technology was used

recent_candidates.title: 'Freed up or congressionally constrained': Is Trump more or less likely to resume war on Iran?
recent_candidates.author: Fleur Hargreaves
recent_candidates.excerpt: 'Freed up or congressionally constrained': Is Trump more or less likely to resume war on Iran? The Democrats secured a sweeping midterm election victory on Tuesday, but one critical question remains unresolved: is US President Donald Trump now more or less likely to resume the war on Iran with the election cycle over? Before the midterms, the US appeared to be on the verge of launching a new, wide-scale attack against Iran. The families of US diplomats were evacuated from the region, and additional US military assets flooded into the Middle East. Arab leaders issued cryptic warnings about a devastating new conflict. But the attack many diplomats and analysts expected around election day never materialised. In fact, Republicans are now blaming the Iran war, and even Israel, for their blistering defeat at the hands of the Democrats. Trump said on Wednesday that "it's largely true" the Iran war and high fuel prices tied to the conflict led to his party’s historic defeat. recent_candidates.title: EU drafts ‘more cautious’ roadmap for Ukraine’s accession, with no timeline for membership, Politico reports
recent_candidates.excerpt: The European Commission has drafted a “more cautious” roadmap for Ukraine’s EU accession talks that sets no target date for membership itself, Politico reported . The outlet said Ukraine’s rapprochement with the EU should be viewed in the context of the country’s postwar future. Brussels sees potential EU membership as a way to anchor Kyiv firmly within European institutions, making it harder for Russia to carry out a new act of aggression. In the new roadmap, Brussels calls on Kyiv to “urgently and significantly step up the pace of the rule of law reforms” in the coming months, before the preliminary stage of accession negotiations on individual policy areas is expected to conclude. The document’s authors expect that Ukraine will complete negotiations on just seven of the 35 clusters by 2027: education and culture, intellectual property, employment and social policy, industrial policy, scientific research, external relations, and security policy. The document also said Ukraine is currently lagging behind Moldova in its progress, a country whose EU application has long been considered alongside Ukraine’s. Moldova is expected to complete negotiations on more than 20 areas by 2027. Ukraine applied for EU membership shortly after Russia launched its full-scale invasion. Unlike with NATO membership, Moscow has never objected to Ukraine joining the European Union. recent_candidates.title: Russian government nearly doubles import duties on hard liquor from ‘unfriendly’ countries
recent_candidates.excerpt: Russia has nearly doubled import duties on hard liquor from “unfriendly” countries. Imported hard liquor will now carry a 35% duty, with a minimum of five euros per liter, up from the previous 20% duty and a three-euro-per-liter floor. The increase is described as a temporary measure, in effect through the end of 2027. The Russian news agency Interfax, citing an explanatory note to the draft federal budget, reported that the higher duties will add 10 billion rubles to the budget in 2027. Russia last changed duties on hard liquor from “unfriendly” countries in 2024, raising the rate from 1.3-1.4 euros per liter to 20% of customs value plus three euros per liter of pure alcohol content. As a result, new duties on cheap beverages in some cases turned out to be lower than before. In September 2026, the government also raised duties on dietary supplements from “unfriendly” countries to 35%, exempting Hungary and Slovakia. Este hallazgo representa uno de los meteoritos marcianos más antiguos jamás encontrados. Lo nombraron Teghaza 001 , en honor a la llanura salina de Malí donde fue descubierto. Actualmente, este meteorito es uno de los 435 ejemplares que proceden de nuestro planeta vecino. Con él, los investigadores de un estudio, publicado en Science, ofrecieron una imagen excepcional de la corteza marciana. En concreto, creen que estos resultados podrían ayudar a responder muchas preguntas, entre ellas cómo interactuaban el agua y las rocas en el planeta rojo. The omission of the 3.8-inch (97mm) medium field gun is harder to explain. Both the French and German armies of 1916 made extensive use of similar weapons: the 105mm gun adopted by the French Army in 1913 and the 10cm guns acquired by German Foot Artillery in 1904 and 1914. Those supplies are often caught in geopolitical crosshairs, as the US and China — locked in a fierce AI race — maneuver to deny each other technological advantages. recent_candidates.author: Alex Jordan
recent_candidates.excerpt: After over four-and-a-half years of entrenched warfare, reports of U.S.-backed peace talks to end Russia's war on Ukraine are back in the news. While Ukrainians arguably thwarted Russian advances in its very first weeks, its backers have failed to help Ukraine consolidate its battlefield victories at the negotiating table. recent_candidates.title: Feijóo aprovecha la Cumbre Iberoamericana para estrechar lazos con Kast y otros líderes
recent_candidates.author: THE OBJECTIVE
recent_candidates.excerpt: El presidente del PP, Alberto Núñez Feijóo , se ha reunido este jueves con el presidente de Chile, José Antonio Kast , para abordar la situación política española y los principales asuntos de actualidad en este periodo preelectoral , según han informado fuentes del Partido Popular a THE OBJECTIVE . Feijóo, que unas horas antes ha mantenido una videoconferencia con la líder de la oposición venezolana, María Corina Machado , ha impulsado su agenda de contactos internacionales coincidiendo con la XXX Cumbre Iberoamericana que se ha celebrado este 4 y 5 de noviembre en Madrid. El encuentro de Feijóo y Kast —al que también asistieron la presidenta del Senado y el presidente de la Cámara de Diputados, además del canciller Francisco Pérez Mackenna— es continuación del que mantuvieron en Lima coincidiendo con la toma de posesión de la presidenta de Perú, Keiko Fujimori. El PP ha subrayado que la relación bilateral con Chile es estratégica para España y ha añadido que la reunión de Feijóo y Kast ha servido para «analizar las oportunidades de inversión en Chile para las empresas españolas que ya tienen una amplia presencia en el país con vocación de permanencia». Asimismo, el presidente Kast ha explicado la situación en Chile tras ocho meses en el Gobierno y los principales retos a los que debe hacer frente tras la gestión del anterior Ejecutivo de izquierdas. Finalmente, hubo un intercambio de opiniones sobre la situación regional en América del Sur, han señalado fuentes ‘populares’.

recent_candidates.excerpt: CCOO ha extendido las huelgas acordadas en el gestor ferroviario ADIF y la empresa pública Renfe del próximo 17 de noviembre a los operadores Iryo y Ouigo con el objetivo de reclamar una mayor seguridad en la red ferroviaria española, han informado a EFE fuentes del sindicato.
